data.name: Mystery P.I.™ - The Lottery Ticket
data.detailed_description:
You are the world-famous Mystery P.I. and you've been hired by Grandma Rose to find her $488 million dollar winning lottery ticket that has gone missing! Retrace Grandma's steps to collect clues by finding hidden objects and solving puzzles. Search the city for the clues and piece them together to solve the case. Grandma Rose has agreed to pay you $20 million if you find the ticket before the deadline. Hurry, you only have 12 hours to find the ticket!
Investigate 20 unique locations to find over 2100 cleverly hidden objects! As your investigation skills improve your P.I. rank increases -- strive for a "Perfect Investigation" to get big bonus points!
Two fun ways to play: In Find the Ticket mode you must locate the missing ticket before the deadline. Unlock Unlimited Seek & Find game mode to search for all the hidden objects with no time limits -- every scene, every item! Collect all 20 KEYS while finding the Ticket to unlock a fun bonus location hidden in the city.

reviews.review:
Mystery P.I.: The Lottery Ticket feels more like a trip down history lane than an actually enjoyable hidden object game in 2026.

The biggest issue is that story is thinner than a razor blade. The setup exists mostly to get you started, and after the introduction, there's practically no narrative motivation to keep you engaged.

The game also shows its age in technical ways. The windowed resolution is tiny by modern standards. On a modern monitor, you'll probably find yourself lowering the display resolution or even creating a custom resolution just to make the game comfortable to play.

Gameplay is repetitive as well. While there are 20 locations, which sounds like a lot, you'll revisit them again and again throughout the game. Hidden object games can get repetitive by nature, but the 5th time you enter the exact same room, you really start to notice how repetitive it feels.

I'm also not a fan of the timed gameplay. One of the main draws of hidden object games is relaxing and searching at your own pace. Constantly glancing at the clock works against that and adds pressure where none is needed.

To the game's credit, it runs on Windows 11 in 2026 without patches, hacks, or workarounds, which is sadly more than can be said for many games from this era. The unlimited mode is also a decent option if you just want to hunt for objects without worrying about progression.

Verdict: Interesting as a relic of the hidden object genre's early days, but difficult to recommend as a game to actually play today. Overall, I'd only recommend Mystery P.I.: The Lottery Ticket to people looking for a dose of nostalgia or those interested in digging in to an early hidden object game as a piece of gaming history. When you start comparing to the plethora of available games, this game falls out of the discussion for a thumbs up.
